newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rally to close at year's high.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rally to close at year's high.

text.p: Driven by bellwether stock YPF, Argentine blue chips rallied Monday and set a new record for 1996, dealers said.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 1.6 percent to 638.26, extending last week's 4.6 percent surge.
"The market trend was fuelled by YPF, which shot up early today on the back of a Morgan Stanley upgrade (to outperform from neutral), said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro.
The oil giant rose 4.0 percent to its highest point this year of $24.65 per share after Morgan Stanley announced the upgrade and forecast higher crude oil and natural gas prices.
Traders said the MerVal, which closed narrowly above the previous 1996 record of 636.58 set December 5, might now face some mild profit taking.

"There may be some erratic falls over the next few days, especially considering volume is likely to shrink to a trickle during tomorrow's short pre-Christmas session and the general strike Thursday," said Alessandro.
The trade unions have called a 24-hour strike against presidential decrees introducing labor reforms.
"I don't think the strike will send jitters through the market, but it's likely to cause a lull," said another trader.
The broad market tacked on 1.1 percent Monday, with risers pounding decliners 49 to five and 14 issues closing unchanged.
Floor volume shrank to 23 million pesos from 29.7 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals recoverd to 117 million pesos from a weak tally of 68.4 million Friday.

Besides YPF, the day's top main-tier performers were power utility Central Costanera, Bansud bank and construction stock Juan Minetti, which jumped 3.2 percent, 3.1 percent and 2.6 percent, respectively. The only MerVal loser was power generator Central Puerto, off 0.4 percent.
